text:
anya: Quick sync — I'm prototyping a "quick-create" flow for A/B experiments in Console. Goal: let product devs spin up a safe experiment in <2 minutes. Need input on routing predicate surface, ramp presets, and quota behavior. TL;DR: propose safe predicate subset + preset ramps + telemetry hooks by default. Thoughts?

oliver: Love the idea. Defaults should be conservative though. Suggest a 3‑step ramp (0 -> 5% -> 25%) with automatic pause/rollback trigger if the primary metric regresses beyond threshold. How do you want metric triggers expressed?

sam: +1 on presets. But, strong objection to automatic metric-driven rollouts in quick-create. Too easy to surprise teams. Keep auto actions off by default; instead attach an "auto-eval" that flags anomalies and suggests rollbacks. Manual confirm for any auto-rollback. Telemetry hooks should be attached by default (baseline + candidate histograms).

ravi: API concern: current ExperimentCreate v1 accepts variant list + weights only. We don't support arbitrary predicate expressions. Adding a free-form predicate string is a security vector (e.g., resource enumeration) and parsing burden. Suggest two options: 1) allow an inline "safe_predicate" with a validated expression subset, or 2) accept a "predicate_id" that references a pre-registered predicate policy. Option 2 is cleaner for ops.

anya: Agreed on safety. Proposal: Console UI exposes simple predicates (hash(user_id)%, country, header runs) and maps them to either inline_safe_predicate or predicate_id depending on user role. Example quick predicate DSL (safe subset):

```yaml
routes:
  - variant: "v2"
    weight: 5
    predicate: "hash(user_id) % 100 < 5 && country == \"US\""
  - variant: "v1"
    weight: 95
    predicate: "true"
```

This keeps it simple for product teams and avoids arbitrary code.

eva: On telemetry: console should auto-wire a small evaluation suite when creating experiments: baseline snapshot + 3 regression checks (p50 latency, p95 latency, success_rate). Also show an estimated cost delta and expected qps per variant so PMs aren't surprised. We should also create a default alert policy: if p95 latency increases >25% for 10m, post to #incidents and halt ramp.

console-bot: experiment-service: created staging experiment id=exp-stg-20260323-9; attached eval suite "quick-defaults".

oliver: About quotas — if a variant causes quota pressure (per-variant QPS cap or reserved capacity exceeded), fallback to the safe variant (default) and mark experiment state as "throttled". UX should show live QPS counters per variant and an obvious cap override button for infra.

sam: UX proposal A vs B: A) Show 3 preset ramps in the wizard (cautious: 0->2->10, standard: 0->10->50, aggressive: 0->25->100 over 24h) with a small description + recommended use cases. B) Advanced toggle to fully customize schedule (timestamped steps). Default to "standard" for quick-create. Also add a tiny inline explainer about deterministic seeding (hash-based) so folks understand repeatability.

ravi: For the API shim: I'll add ExperimentCreate v1.1 that accepts either "predicate_id" or "inline_safe_predicate". Server validates inline predicates against the allowed ops and compiles them to a predicate bytecode. Will include backwards-compatible migration and a feature flag.

anya: Decision summary: (1) implement safe predicate subset + predicate_id reference for advanced users; (2) ship ramp presets + default to "standard"; (3) attach telemetry evals and estimated cost by default but keep auto-rollback off for quick-create; (4) expose per-variant QPS/cap with fallback to safe variant on quota breach; (5) API v1.1 with server-side validation. I'll open an RFC and break into tasks. cc @ravi to own the API shim, @eva to own telemetry wiring.

ravi: ACK — will start a draft API PR and include validation tests.

anya: Thanks team — I'll put the RFC in #eng-platform and tag for review. :rocket:
